title: Update Published Alert
description:
Update a published Collaborate alert in the Analyst Portal by expiring the older alert and linking it to this new alert.

### Changelog


Supports scheduling and updating alert expiry using the scheduled_expiry_time parameter.
Access to certain categories is based on your user role in the Analyst Portal. This update does not impact credentials generated prior to this version.


### Alert Field Types


As an analyst, you can create alerts using custom fields tailored to your needs. Use fields like text boxes for detailed input, multi-select for tagging multiple values, single-select for predefined choices, and more to customize your alerts effectively. For details on retrieving additional field information, see the Retrieve Additional Fields section. Use the table below for custom field format:
Field Type
Description
Structure
Boolean
Boolean fields allow you to select either true or false for specific options. While creating an alert, you can use these fields to indicate details such as whether the alert is Publicly Shareable or Requires Immediate Action.
field_id: value
Example:
"f65b26a174658": true
Text
Text boxes allow you to add information in text format. While creating an alert, you can use these fields to provide details such as Threat Description, Likely Motivation, and more.
field_id: Text
Example:
"f533606babb44": "CVE-2014-12345"
Single-select
Single-select fields allow you to choose one option from a predefined list. These fields are used to capture key details of an alert, such as Threat Level or Severity.
field_id: { field_id_id: selected value id}
Example:
Example: "ffa80c88f1d20": { "ffa80c88f1d20_id": "oaa822c36c133" }
Multi-select
Multi-select fields allow you to associate multiple options with an alert from a predefined list. For example, you can use these fields to assign Affected Sectors or Indicators.
field_id: [{ field_id+_id: selected value id}, { field_id+_id: selected value id}]
Example:
"f65b26a174658": [ { "f65b26a174658_id": "o15f317d51bec" }, { "f65b26a174658_id": "o43d57e02d92a" } ]
Date & Time
Date and time fields let you capture time-sensitive details for an alert, such as Reported At or Action Deadline. The values are stored in Epoch (Unix timestamp) format.
field_id: EPOCH value
Example:
"f9c217dfe8824": 1709725603

Additional fields are custom or system fields that you can use while creating alerts. To ensure accurate field mapping, you need to retrieve additional field IDs and details before passing them as body parameters. To retrieve field details, follow these steps:
1.  Use the **Get Additional Fields List** endpoint in the Alerts section to retrieve the list of all fields, including their field IDs.
2.  Use the `field_id` in the **Get Additional Fields Details** endpoint to retrieve associated field details.

body.name: short_id
body.description: Pass the unique ID of the alert that you want to update. You can use the **Get Alerts** endpoint to retrieve the ID.

body.name: title
body.description: Pass the title of the alert. Example: *New Malware Variant Targeting Enterprise Networks*.
body.value: New Malware Variant Targeting Enterprise Networks

body.name: content
body.description: Pass the description for the alert.
body.value: A newly discovered malware strain is actively exploiting vulnerabilities in enterprise networks, enabling unauthorized access and data exfiltration. Organizations are advised to update security measures, monitor network traffic, and apply patches to mitigate the threat.

body.name: is_content_defanged
body.description: Pass true to specify that the link is not clickable.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Pass the custom fields associated with the alert, as these may vary based on the selected alert category.

items.name: f159dc38f3255
items.description: Pass the ID of the custom field.

body.name: card_image
body.description: Pass the URL for the alert image. Ensure the `type` parameter is URL. Example: *https://cyware.com/cyware.jpg*. To pass `card_image`, ensure you also pass the following type field.

body.name: type
body.description: Pass the type of alert image.

body.name: card_info
body.description:
Pass any additional details in HTML format. Example: Adversary:,
Malware Families: njRAT, AsyncRAT, Houdini RAT
Attack IDs: T1104, T1547
body.value:
Adversary:,

body.name: card_category
body.description: Pass the category for the alert. You can retrieve the list of available alert categories using the **Get Category List** endpoint. You can only enter a category that is associated with your user role in the Analyst Portal. To assign a category to the alert, pass either the `card_category` or `card_category_name` parameter. `card_category` takes precedence if both are passed.

items.name: category_id
items.description: Pass the unique ID of the category associated with the alert.

items.name: category_name
items.description: Pass the name of the category associated with the alert.

body.name: card_category_name
body.description: Pass the category for the alert. You can only enter a category that is associated with your user role in the Analyst Portal. Note: To assign category to the alert, pass either the `card_category` or `card_category_name` parameters. `card_category` takes precedence if both are passed.

body.name: content
body.description: Returns the description of the alert.
body.value: We have tracked a unique and ongoing RAT delivery campaign that started in February of this year. This campaign is unique in that it heavily uses the AutoHotKey scripting language-a fork of the AutoIt language that is frequently used for testing purposes. Starting in February, we have identified at least four versions of the RAT delivery campaign, each of which includes multiple advancements and adaptations over the past three months. This blog post dives into the details of each attack chain, while highlighting interesting and rare techniques that the attackers use.
